### Comment 1

<code_context>
 ) {
 	const query = `
-		SELECT * FROM ${OPENLIT_CRON_LOG_TABLE_NAME} WHERE cron_id = '${cronId}' AND run_status = '${CronRunStatus.SUCCESS}'
+		SELECT started_at AS startedAt FROM ${OPENLIT_CRON_LOG_TABLE_NAME} WHERE cron_id = '${cronId}' AND run_status = '${CronRunStatus.SUCCESS}'
 		ORDER BY started_at DESC
 		LIMIT 1
</code_context>
<issue_to_address>
**Eligible spans are skipped**

When an external source has more eligible spans than one `listSpans` page returns, the external-source fetchers request at most 500 spans (Jaeger caps a page at 200) and do not fetch subsequent pages, while the jobs can still log success. The next checkpoint advances past the unreturned spans, so they are never evaluated or priced.

Fetch all pages before recording a successful checkpoint, or otherwise keep the checkpoint from advancing past unprocessed spans.
</issue_to_address>

### Comment 2
<location path="src/client/src/lib/platform/cron-log/index.ts" line_range="126" />
<code_context>
 ) {
 	const query = `
-		SELECT * FROM ${OPENLIT_CRON_LOG_TABLE_NAME} WHERE cron_id = '${cronId}' AND run_status = '${CronRunStatus.SUCCESS}'
+		SELECT started_at AS startedAt FROM ${OPENLIT_CRON_LOG_TABLE_NAME} WHERE cron_id = '${cronId}' AND run_status = '${CronRunStatus.SUCCESS}'
 		ORDER BY started_at DESC
 		LIMIT 1
</code_context>
<issue_to_address>
**Lookback shifts across timezones**

When an external telemetry source is used and the Node process timezone differs from the ClickHouse server timezone, clickHouse serializes this `DateTime` without a timezone offset, but the external-source paths in `fetchAutoEvalCandidateSpans` and `fetchAutoPricingCandidateSpans` pass the string to `new Date(lastRunIso)`, which interprets it in the Node process timezone. When that differs from the ClickHouse timezone, the lookback boundary shifts and traces are skipped or reprocessed.

Return or normalize the timestamp with an explicit timezone before passing it to JavaScript date parsing.
</issue_to_address>
~~~

</details>

Reviewer's guide (collapsed on small PRs) ## Reviewer's Guide The PR fixes last-successful-cron-run retrieval by mapping ClickHouse’s `started_at` column to the client’s `startedAt` property and treating empty results as no prior run. Regression tests cover both fresh crons with no successful run and historical runs, preventing failures in Auto Evaluation and auto pricing callers. #### Sequence diagram for corrected last successful cron run lookup ```mermaid sequenceDiagram participant Caller as AutoEvaluationOrPricing participant CronLog as getLastRunCronLogByCronId participant ClickHouse Caller->>CronLog: getLastRunCronLogByCronId(cronId) CronLog->>ClickHouse: SELECT started_at AS startedAt ... LIMIT 1 ClickHouse-->>CronLog: data alt no successful run or query error CronLog-->>Caller: null Caller->>Caller: use no previous run else successful run found CronLog-->>Caller: data[0].startedAt Caller->>Caller: use lastRunTime end ``` ### File-Level Changes | Change | Details | Files | | ------ | ------- | ----- | | Make last successful cron-run lookup safe for empty results and return the correctly shaped timestamp field. |
  • Select `started_at` with the `startedAt` alias expected by the client.
  • Return `null` when the query result is empty, null, or errored.
  • Preserve the existing latest-successful-run ordering and limit.
| `src/client/src/lib/platform/cron-log/index.ts` | | Add regression coverage for missing runs and timestamp aliasing. |
  • Verify an empty result returns `null` without throwing.
  • Verify the query uses the alias and the aliased timestamp is returned.
  • Retain coverage for null data and query errors.
| `src/client/src/__tests__/lib/platform/cron-log/cron-log.test.ts` | ### Assessment against linked issues | Issue | Objective | Addressed | Explanation | | ------ | ------- | ----- | ----- | | https://github.com/openlit/openlit/issues/1867 | Handle an empty successful Cron execution history without crashing, so Auto Evaluation can continue processing eligible traces. | ✅ | |
